text:
maria: FYI started kyoto-v1 onboard + q4a bring-up on staging, throwing the usual multilingual holdout set at it. results look... weird.
ken: weird how? numbers or tokens?
li: saw the short summary in the run artifacts — Japanese vertical samples BLEU down ~3.2 vs baseline, and some CJK detok diffs.
maria: exact: BLEU dev-ja-vertical: baseline 28.7 -> kyoto-v1-int8 25.5. also token deltas: sequences with furigana/inline ruby get split differently.
devon: hmm could be tokenizer vocabulary mismatch after quant kernel changes. did you run the tokenizer-only regression (no quant) to isolate?
maria: yes — kyoto-v1-fp16 (no quant) keeps BLEU ~28.4. so it's tied to quant path or runtime detok.
ken: are we sure it's not KV-cache streaming change interacting with hyphenation? we changed KVCACHE flush timing in the q4a runtime.
li: i grep'd examples: lines where vertical ruby present show extra <unk> tokens in the int8 output stream. also some RTL samples (Arabic) show bracket direction flips when using the int8 binary.
maria: posted a few examples in the artifact: https://ci.redwood/example/kyoto-v1/1717654321/artifacts (see files: ja_vertical_examples.txt, ar_bracket_flip.txt)
eval-bot: snapshot: kyoto-v1-int8 staging run | BLEU: ja-vertical 25.5 (-3.2) | ja-ltr 28.9 (-0.1) | zh 31.1 (+0.2) | ar-rtl 22.0 (-1.4) | token-diff-rate 0.93% | detok-errors 42
maria: token-diff-rate seems small but concentrated on combo scripts (ruby + zwj + punctuation).
devon: can you paste the minimal repro snippet? maybe a short prompt that fails reproducibly.
maria: sure — here's one that shows the split:```
入力: 漢字(ふりがな)テスト。
Expected detok: 漢字ふりがなテスト。
Int8 detok: 漢字 ( ふりがな ) テスト 。
```
li: that's classic: spacing/token-insert around parentheses. maybe the postprocessor unicode-nfkc normalization order changed in the quant path. Also check bidi markers insertion for Arabic.
ken: q4a quant pipeline patches touched the token->detokenize hook where we apply locale-specific rules. maybe a race where streaming flush calls detok earlier.
maria: repro on staging with --no-stream -> int8 still shows the spacing issue (so not streaming-only).
devon: could be kernel-level token id mapping shift for rare tokens (ZWJ, LEFT PAREN, RUBY OPEN). if quantized embedding table had an index shift during packing that would explain it.
li: i ran a quick token-id diff between fp16 and int8 exporter:
```
# summary output
mismatched_ids: [6521: U+200D, 9412: U+3008]
# most mismatches map to punctuation/zwj/paren
```
li: looks like packing script's reserve slot math overflowed for vocab size % 512.
ken: ok good find. can we hotfix packer and re-export? what's the release window?
maria: i can try a repack+export to staging later today, but we should add a targeted unit test for mixed ruby+zwj cases.
devon: also add a small ablation: export int8 with and without packer optimization flag (--preserve-indices) to confirm.
li: i'll open a PR with failing test & fix. tag me and @maria for validation.
maria: thanks. for tracking: creating a short eval holdout specifically for 'ruby+zwj+paren' combos and Arabic bracket-direction samples. will run full holdout after repack.
eval-bot: created regression ticket #ML-5891 with artifacts and failing examples.
ken: nice. if that packer fix fixes token ids, expect BLEU to recover close to fp16 for ja-vertical. keep an eye on ar-rtl bracket flips though. might need bidi marker ordering fix in postprocessing.
li: quick todo: 1) repack/export int8 with preserve-indices 2) run targeted holdout 3) add unit test for ruby+ZWJ 4) verify Arabic bracket order 5) if green, promote to canary.
maria: sounds good. i'll run step 1 tonight and post results. thx :thumbsup:
devon: ping if you need infra for faster parallel holdout runs, i can spin up a few more workers.
li: thanks. logging the thread here so we don't lose examples.
maria: added one more note: observed slight latency improvement on int8 (~12%) which is nice if we can fix quality. tradeoff worth it.
ken: perfect. keep updates here.
